prompt:
A THREE-panel strip about running your own launch-reward campaign instead of renting a platform that keeps a copy of your participant list.
STRIP LAYOUT: a horizontal MULTIPANEL STRIP of three equal-width panels in one row on a warm cream ground, separated by clean cream gutters with NO drawn borders and NO frame lines. The panels read left to right as one continuous argument, in ONE consistent room, with ONE consistent cast and ONE consistent glowing translucent amber laptop.
COMPOSITION LAW: the campaign machinery and all small figures are INSIDE the glowing amber laptop screen, small and warmly lit. The human stays in the warm real world outside the laptop, at her desk, and the human supplies the judgment.
FIGURE DISCIPLINE: the same human appears in every panel and must be recognizably the same person in each, same face, same hair, same clothing.
ABSOLUTELY NOT: a denim jacket, a jean jacket, any chest patch, any smiley-face badge, any enamel pin, any embroidered emblem, a white tee under an open jacket. No recurring branded character and no identifiable real individual. No armor, no power suit, no superhero costume, no helmet, no visor.
THE HUMAN: a woman in her forties with olive skin and dark brown hair in a low bun, wearing a plain rust-colored cardigan over a grey shirt.
BEAT ONE: inside the glowing laptop, a queue of small people hand a card each to a tall impassive clerk standing at a counter. The clerk drops every card into a deep cabinet behind him and slides only ONE thin slip forward, out of the screen, to the woman at her desk. The wooden shelf beside her desk is empty. She looks at the single slip.
BEAT TWO: same room, same desk, same laptop. Inside the glowing laptop the clerk, the counter and the cabinet are all gone; a rounded agent figure in a gold military cap stands beside a simple upright panel with exactly THREE tall checkboxes, ticking them one after another, and each small person's card travels straight out of the screen and stacks onto the wooden shelf beside her desk, which is now filling up. She watches the shelf fill.
BEAT THREE: she sits back at the desk holding up one plain card marked with a single bold wordless ink stroke. Inside the glowing laptop, FOUR small people standing in a close ring each hold a coupon and pass that same ink stroke outward to a much larger crowd standing beyond the ring who hold no coupons at all and carry it on.
TEXT FURNITURE, render each string EXACTLY, in caps, in the cream margin and never over the artwork:
Title bar above the panels: OWN THE INCENTIVE LOOP
Caption in the cream gutter under panel one: THE PLATFORM KEEPS THE LIST
Caption in the cream gutter under panel two: YOUR PAGE, YOUR LIST
Caption in the cream gutter under panel three: CONVICTION CARRIES IT FURTHER
Footer bar below the panels: BUILD THE LOOP. KEEP THE PEOPLE.
NO OTHER TEXT ANYWHERE. Every card, coupon, slip, cabinet front, checkbox panel and screen is BLANK apart from wordless ink marks. There are no signs, no labels, no logos, no shop names, no door plaques.

warm editorial illustration, soft painterly line and gentle shading, muted natural palette on a warm cream ground, grounded and human, picture-book register for adults

Do NOT render it in any of these styles: comic-book, cartoon mascot, flat vector, neon, 3D/CGI/Pixar, photoreal, anime, any identifiable recurring individual's face or signature clothing.

These are LOCKED canonical traits of the subject(s). They are not stylistic suggestions and must survive the render exactly: small-blocky-clay-coral-orange-mascot; translucent-holographic-digital-being; casts-light-not-shadow; grand-ornate-gold-admiral-hat; gold-epaulettes; warm-rounded-dot-eyes-with-tiny-catchlights; two-stubby-legs; short-stubby-nub-arms-end-in-rounded-MITTEN-stubs-NEVER-fingers-hands-tubes-or-bars; never-LIVES-in-the-real-world-soft-crossing-allowed-only-at-delivery-leaning-through-the-screen-body-mostly-inside; never-over-anthropomorphized; never-does-task-work-only-listens-commands-delivers; warm-editorial-register-not-comic.

Identity of record is reference/chief-of-agents/master.png. Derive EVERY new pose from it (pass master as the FIRST input image), one pose per render; NEVER a multi-pose sheet in a single generation (that drifts the body composition). Keep it a SMALL blocky mascot: clay-coral Anthropic orange (~#D97757), two dot-eyes, two stubby legs, a grand ornate GOLD admiral hat + gold epaulettes (this is what makes it the Chief; sub-agents wear plain white sailor caps, no gold). It is a DIGITAL being: translucent, holographic, glowing, casts LIGHT not shadow, lives inside the computer / the agentverse. Do NOT over-anthropomorphize — no big arms, no human proportions (that was the rejected creepy variant). It never does task work; it only listens, commands, and delivers. CROSSING LAW (Gary 2026-07-16, clarified same day): the Chief never LIVES in the real world; it never stands on a real desk, sits in a real chair, or walks a real room as a free-standing body. The one permitted SOFT CROSSING is delivery: leaning through the screen plane, body mostly inside, to hand an artifact to the human or receive one; artifacts themselves may pass through the glass. Delivery may equally be drawn as work materializing on the screen. emerging.png and delivering.png depict the soft-crossing grammar and remain canon references. LONE-AGENT LAW (Gary 2026-07-16): when a scene shows exactly ONE agent, it is the Chief.
